models.inverse_notes: annual is linear given rate and years (exact rational-polynomial view). rate has no exact view: substitution gives degree above two, so exact solving reports unsupported_degree (verified against the source-3-shaped model, which preserves that diagnostic for lack of a finite bracket); with the rate <= 0.1 ceiling the finite bracket (0, 0.1] admits scan-then-bisection, which recovers 0.0300034523 from the published NIST Table 5-3 case (8000, 20 yr, PV 119016) in 1,112 evaluations. years is period_count, so the equal-relation view enumerates the guarded integers 1..100. Substitution check at years = 1 gives annual / (1 + rate) (verified to 1e-13). The rate-to-0 limit branch PV = annual * years is a different expression, never a guard relaxation.

references.method: Published NIST Table 5-2 row: $7,000/yr OM&R over 20 yr at the 3% real FEMP rate prices at UPV factor 14.877, giving $104,139; the closed form gives 104,142.32 and the tolerance covers the table's 3-decimal factor rounding. Cross-checked by summing twenty individual discounted cash flows.

references.method: Published UMD worked example: A=100, i=10%, n=8 gives P=533.49; the closed form gives 533.4926. Cross-checked by summing eight individual discounted cash flows. The 10% rate sits exactly at the published ceiling, so this oracle also exercises the guard boundary.

references.method: Published NIST Table 5-3 case ($8,000/yr, 20 yr, PV $119,016 at 3% real) recomputed by solving for rate: scan-then-bisection over the guarded bracket (0, 0.1] returns 0.0300034523 in 1,112 evaluations (solver output residual 7.0e-05); independent Newton solve gives 0.030003452365 (forward residual 1.5e-07), matching the published 3% to four decimals; the offset reflects the table's 3-decimal factor rounding. Forward replay at the published 3% gives 119,019.80, within the rounding tolerance. r1 correction: the r1 8-decimal quote 0.03000345 has forward residual 2.6e-03, not 7.1e-05 as stated.

rejection_cases.reason: Periodic rate 150% exceeds the 10%-per-period published ceiling (rate <= 0.1); no published FEMP case approaches this regime.
Periodic rate 100% exceeds the 10% ceiling (rate <= 0.1): the r1 100% envelope boundary is outside the published FEMP application scope (10 CFR 436 caps the real DOE rate at 10%).
Zero rate makes the divisor zero and needs the separate limit branch PV = annual * years; excluded by rate > 0 (byte-identical to source-3).
Negative discount rates are outside the FEMP scope and excluded by rate > 0 (byte-identical to source-3).
Zero years is an empty series; excluded by years >= 1 (byte-identical to source-3).
Horizons beyond 100 years exceed the study-period scope; excluded by years <= 100 (byte-identical to source-3).
Term count years is required; the horizon is undefined without it.

relationship.locator: Interest Formulae: Equal-Payment-Series Present-Worth Factor (boxed factor; Example 1 with A=100, i=10%, n=8 giving P=533.49).
relationship.translation_notes: UMD symbols map A -> annual, i -> rate, n -> years, P -> pv; the boxed factor is transcribed verbatim into scalar syntax. Dimensional check: USD times a dimensionless factor stays USD. Guards rate > 0, years >= 1, years <= 100 are byte-identical to uniform-present-value@source-3; rate <= 0.1 encodes the 10 CFR 436 ceiling on the real DOE discount rate (NIST HB 135 section 3.3.2, PDF p. 67/printed p. 35), matching the published FEMP scope whose Chapter 5 cases price at the 3% floor. NIST HB 135 is the application and scope authority: its published UPV values (Tables 5-2 to 5-5) are reproduced by this expression.

sources.evidence: PDF verified live (DOI 10.6028/NIST.HB.135-2020): section 3.2.2.1 defines the UPV factor with Eq. 3-7 and a $100/5yr/3%=$457.97 worked example (recomputed 457.9707); section 3.3.2 states 10 CFR 436 bounds the real DOE discount rate between 3% and 10%; Table 5-1 sets the FEMP criteria (real DOE discount rate, end-of-year cash flows, constant dollars); section 5.1.2 introduces UPV factors for annually recurring costs; Table 5-2 prices $7,000/yr OM&R over 20 yr at UPV(3%) = 14.877 giving $104,139; Table 5-3 prices $8,000/yr at the same factor giving $119,016; section 8.6.6.1 names UPV the uniform present value of an annuity. Chapter 5 examples use the 3% real DOE rate (floor binding since 2004); section 8.6.6 uses a 2.15% non-DOE real rate.
